newsitem.title: GERMANY: Old crop rapeseed supply thinning in North Europe.
newsitem.headline: Old crop rapeseed supply thinning in North Europe.

text.p: Traders and crushers are looking for some old crop rapeseed in northern Europe at firm prices but supplies are running out fast, brokers said on Friday.
Prices also took support from high Chicago soycomplex values, a strong dollar and some oil business as competing sun oil also gained in price, they said.
"Demand is exceeding supply on the old crop while new crop negotiations are still slow," one broker said.
Brokers put trade buyers of old crop at 502-505 marks a tonne free Hamburg with crushers at 507.
New crop buyers free Hamburg were in the low 460s, basis August, with monthly increments implied at three to four marks thereafter.
May seed buyers at points other than Hamburg 490-515 marks range, some 15-20 marks above prices a fortnight ago, with June free Salzgitter quoted at 512.50.
Germany has not shared the weather concerns of some other western European countries, where drought has threatened to undermine grains and oilseeds yields for the 1997 harvest.
But temperatures are too cold for the time of year and need watching, traders said. Winter damage to rapeseed was minimal.
May rapeseed futures on Matif exchange last traded at 517 marks, up six and Aug at 460 marks, off two.
Spot April rape meal ex Hamburg mills was offered little changed at 32.50-32.75 marks per 100 kg, with May-first half July at 32.25 and Aug-Oct at 26.75.
Local rape oil sellers were two marks up per 100 kg on the last fortnight. April was quoted at 92.50 marks per 100 kg, May-July at 93.50 and Aug-Oct at 92.50.
